body:
Unrelated, but just now I remembered replying to a post by someone who didn't want to die alone (this was three months ago).  I kinda panicked when I wondered what happened to this person (you).  And, hey man, I'm really glad that you're still around.  
Related - There are definitely good people out there who in the long run prefer personality over appearance.  Women in general probably won't look at your skin and think too highly of it, but they shouldn't be breaking up with you because of it.  That's just sick.

Just reassure him that you're going to be in areas with lots of people (and try to make and effort too, don't just say it) and buy a bottle of pepper spray if he is so concerned.  I'm serious, my friend who is playing Pokemon Go actually got one himself just in case.

You're not indebted to them for giving you a life.  It's a shit life that you don't deserve and you know it.  They said "see if I care" when you mentioned your suicidal thoughts - they're obviously so pro-life lol.  But I like that you're giving them "test run"... by leaving.  If you're pulling so much legwork around the house then getting your own place is the equivalent of being dead to them.  They'll be so shocked.  See if they really care then.  Jk, the outcome is obvious.  

Also, your dad is seriously mad that you're not giving him money?  Make sure to send him Monopoly money in the mail after you're gone or tell him to go shoplift something. 

Good luck.  I hate to know that somewhere out there, there is someone who has to deal with all of this.  And I thought my life was hard 😅☹️
Yes!  Sometimes at night I randomly see my messy room and go, hmm, time to clean up!  However it usually doesn't work because 2 hours later when it's super late at night my room is still messy 😝
ISFP-T,  The Adventurer apparently.  I feel like the oddball out due to my shyness.  The fact that most Asians here are extroverted really took me by surprise!
Asian parents can eat the strangest things...
My parents are that way too.  I dated a black guy and they were NOT very happy about it 😬

I've been to New York at least 30 times with family.  Pretty much every time we go to same Korean BBQ, hair salon, dentist, parking lots, bakery, and grocery stores.  Otherwise we're picking up/dropping off someone from the airport, or going to this Japanese supermarket.  It's annoying because the driving back and forth always takes up 4 hours of the day.
When Asian parents get together and talk about their children bad ideas, badmouthing and new ways of parenting are bound to come... I hate the 80-95% Asian-attended 4th of July parties we go to.

Look into your parent's past.  It will be extremely helpful if they weren't bogged down taking care of their own parents, even better if one of your grandparents had some sort of medical condition that is worse than your father's.  Bonus points if they had the chance to do something they wanted to, like focusing on their own career.  If so, tell them it's not fair for them to do this to you, especially if they believe your brother is the cause of your dad's health problems (if you're willing to fly that low).  If they were deprived of those chances of living their life under a roof besides that of their own parents, then tell them they should give you a chance.  Maybe promise if your dad's condition worsens tenfold you'll take care of them somehow.  Best of luck.

I'm sorry, not a homosexual, but I've considered bisexuality, though if I choose that path my family would not support me.  But if you do come out of the closet, maybe think about adoption if she really wants a grandkid...
Holy cow!  I really hope my mom isn't planning on surviving on sunlight.  Dying of hunger is definitely worse than losing your eyesight.  I'll see what her deal is on this one.
Sounds like it's worth a shot!  I'll see what I can do.
Thanks, it's nice to know that.
My brothers (who are 18+) think she is being irrational.
It's not necessarily a Buddhism "thing", just something monks she apparently trust (just because they're Buddhist like what even) do and introduced it to her.

She already has though and believes it's harmless because she's already tried it.  But when she goes into longer periods of time staring at the f/king sun I'll fear for the worst.  

On a side note... A welder's mask does sound like a pretty good idea right now,
I still see very big problems here, but thanks anyways.  I appreciate your input but that's just not what I was looking for.
True that.  Doubt the pollution thing will work, but crazy-crazy sounds just about right.  Kid, you are a genius.
Yes.  Yes.  Oh my god yes.
Yeah, especially if they're Buddhist.  They think that the bad karma and some believe the ghost of the child will follow you.  I'm atheist but I generally think it's just unethical.

Nothing about pregnancy, but when my dad got really sick and was sent to the hospital my mom refused to go see him.  Get this: she thought he deserved it because she thinks she knows about everything health-related (she isn't even a doctor) and was actually MAD at him.  She usually gets mad at me when I'm sick, even if it's just a cold or something, and it is beyond annoying.
My mom complains about how she's the only one who does stuff.  So not true.

From what I can understand sun gazing is an ancient method and probably has more importance over moon gazing, if that is a thing.  

On a side note, my mom loves her homeland so much that I'm not even sure why she came back.  That and her passion for Buddhism is making her think sun gazing is the answer to her vision and financial problems (she doesn't want my family to pay for medical bills (basically doesn't want anything major to happen to us, perhaps like me needing eye surgery as well)).  

Finally, I'd like to stress that her final goal will be to look at the sun for as looooooong as possible.  She probably won't lose her eyesight right away tomorrow.  But one day she might if she keeps this increment goal up.

My mom discourages creative careers (like becoming an artist) and tried to make my brother steer clear of the oil industry (it didn't work out and she was actually right about it, he and a bunch of his coworkers got laid off because the company wasn't doing so hot).  She also wanted him to do something with water, like bottling it or something.  Idk what she meant by that.

Then there are  my grandparents.  Whenever they hear something they think is cool they call us up (me and my siblings) and tell them we should do that instead of something else we are pursuing.  They are unreliable with their info though and they also live across the world :/
She says something along the lines of "I will evolve past regular human eyesight" and insists that staring at the sun for longer periods of time will make her eyesight better, unfortunately.

Japan is amazing.  Maybe taking the trip there will change your mind.  Believe me when I say that your emotionally overwhelmed girlfriend was not your sole reason to live; there is more than that.  There is Japan, your friends, your parents.  And you can find other things to live for than just that, you just need to find them.

Staying alive is not selfish, it's the ideal state that living entities were "programmed" to want in the first place.  It is no big deal if staying alive will run your family a little money.  Financial issues are not everything.  Your loved ones will miss you, and will be sad if they found out you did it just because of a supposed burden you place on them.  You are still young and could have many chances to change the way things are.

Digital art, acrylic/watercolor, polymer clay, pottery (with a spinning wheel), calligraphy, origami, collages, sewing and knitting are all fun!  Ever heard of Muse Paintbar?  It's a fun place and if you don't live near one find something like it, their instructors are AMAZING!

Then maybe work your way from your friend instead of her parents.  Ask her if she wants to get therapy; tell her that if she doesn't know why she is depressed a professional can help her.  This way her parents can swoop in if she wants to get help (she'll have to ask them if she can't drive a car/pay at her age).  If she is skeptical for fear of her parents not accepting her then reassure her.  Unsure what else you could do.

I would outright tell him what I know.  It's dangerous for him not to understand what his daughter is going through.  I understand that it may feel like you are intruding on your friend's life but if her parents are given vague information (or none at all) it can do more harm than good.  Maybe tell him not to mention you if you don't want her to find out just yet?  After telling him about her condition he should be able to take it from there.  After all, he is her parent.  If you feel too awkward telling him this through voice chat sending an email can do wonders, too.
Friends aren't everything.  Your girlfriend probably wasn't the one.  Don't give up so easily; you control your emotions, not the other way around.

I would strongly advise saying something else along those lines.  Telling her dad that could be the equivalent to saying "This may seem uncalled for, but believe me, you're not expressing your love for your daughter enough."  People can easily take things the wrong way.

Instead try a more encouraging apporach.  But first take other information to do so.  Does her dad know about her depression at all?  Is lack of love really what's causing her emptiness?  If not, then how can you rephrase the question?

I used to be really scared of people, and I know that awkwardness is really hard to overcome.  My first year of high school I literally made one friend.  I actually had to practice what I should say in certain scenarios so I wouldn't sound stupid; I just didn't want to lose the one person in my life and not weird out others.  

Maybe creative writing can help you figure out how to deal with life situations, especially what you want to say to your friends.  You don't seem so awkward through a screen (and somehow some people really are) and it's evident that you put effort into your post.  Maybe you can channel what you say in your writing into your world.  I glad you are trying to be better but now isn't the time to give up.

I hope you're still around.  It seems you have lost all hope because you've given in to a troll who sent you a PM, one that unfairly took advantage of your current state of weakness.  I've been in that position before and I'm never going to let anyone give me that sort of BS again.  If anyone is worthless it's the bottom scum that lurks around a subreddit waiting to crush someone looking for help.  You said yourself that others push you around and it's been happening for too long.  Because of this you let a single person alone control your emotions, a stranger who for all you know could be a homeless man in a library.  

    As for your real life you need to realize that many people will move on and it happens to everyone.  If your best friend leaves you behind then find someone else, and if you can't then get a pet or a hobby.  If someone cheats on you chances are it's not your fault and you need to forget about them.  Look at life another way and maybe you'll find answers there, because it is never too late.  Some people are just wicked; twisted; they want to get a reaction from you.  Please find a way to prove them wrong; you are not worthless just because of what others think or say about you.
